newsitem.title: CANADA: Shell Canada profits soar after chemical sale.
newsitem.headline: Shell Canada profits soar after chemical sale.

text.p: Shell Canada Ltd., the Canadian energy arm of giant Royal Dutch/Shell Group, reported sharply higher fourth-quarter earnings on Wednesday after a major gain from the sale of its chemical business.
Shell Canada's earnings for the quarter rose to C$342 million ($253 million) or C$3.05 ($2.26) a share from year earlier C$75 million ($56 million) or C67 cents (50 cents) a share.
Fourth-quarter revenues jumped to C$1.5 billion ($1.1 billion) from C$1.1 billion ($814 million) in the same period of the previous year.

Shell Canada is a major oil producer and holder of oil, natural gas and sulphur reserves in Western Canada and is one of Canada's three national gasoline retailers. Late last year it sold its chemical division for C$635 million ($470 million) for a gain of C$226 million ($167 million).
The operation was acquired by a unit of Anglo-Dutch parent Royal Dutch/Shell, which owns 78 percent of Shell Canada.
For the full year, Shell Canada posted net earnings of C$595 million ($440 million) or C$5.30 ($3.92) a share, up from C$523 million ($387 million) or C$4.66 ($3.45) a share in 1995.
The company said its cash war chest ballooned to almost C$1.2 billion ($888 million) at the end of 1996 from C$444 million ($329 million) the year before.

Shell Canada spokeswoman Jan Rowley said the company's projected investments in the planned multi-partner Sable Island natural gas project off the Canadian east coast province of Nova Scotia and a proposed oil sands development in northeastern Alberta were likely candidates for much of the cash.
She said the oil sands project, still in the design stage, could be valued "in the billions" of dollars.
Shell Canada shares were down C25 cents to C$53.25 in Toronto on Wednesday.
